senses.gloss: m. (לָקַט) collection.—Esp. ל׳ עצמות, or לִיקּוּטֵי the gathering of bones, i.e. the transfer of a body from the provisional cave to a permanent burial place, at which certain mourning ceremonies are to be observed by the nearest relatives; v. לָקַט.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 8:8:6">Y. Pes. VIII, 36ᵇ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:5:4">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵈ</cite> top <he>המעביר … אין בו משום ל׳ ע׳</he> he who transfers a coffin from one burial place to another need not observe the ceremonies connected with the transfer of bones.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:5:4">Ib.</cite> <he>איזיהו ל׳ ע׳ וכ׳</he> what is ‘bone-collection’ in a ritual sense? Carrying a skeleton wrapped &c., v. <cite ref="A02789"><he>אַפְקַרְסִין</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>לִיקּוּטִין</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:6:9">Y. Peah IV, end, 18ᶜ</cite> <he>קל … בל׳</he> the scholars have adopted the lighter (less stringent) practice with reference to the collections (by the poor, v. <cite ref="L00679"><he>לֶקֶט</he></cite>).—<he>לִיקּוּטֵי עצמות</he>, v. supra.
